desc:
'We have found the Messiah' (which is translated as Christ) (John 1:41): the text glosses Messiah as Christ (also John 4:25). Who in the text says that Jesus is the Christ, and in whose words, is on this card: the narrators and authors; Peter, Andrew, Martha, an angel and Paul; and Jesus' own answers when asked (Mark 14:62; John 4:26; Matt 26:64).

Luke gives no yes to the question: asked 'If You are the Christ, tell us', Jesus answers 'If I tell you, you will not believe. And if I ask you a question, you will not answer' (Luke 22:67-68); to the next question, 'Are You then the Son of God?', 'You say that I am' (22:70), and the council says, 'Why do we need any more testimony?' (22:71).
disambiguation: the title as the text uses it of Jesus, with whose words each use is
name: the Christ

desc: 'Just then an angel of the Lord stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them' (Luke 2:9); he tells the shepherds of the birth: 'He is Christ the Lord!' (Luke 2:11). The text does not name him.
disambiguation: the angel who appeared to the shepherds (Luke 2:9-12); the text does not name him or say he is the angel of the LORD of the Old Testament
name: an angel of the Lord (to the shepherds)
